# Chairperson 

The club chair is the principal officer for the club and is elected by the club 
members.

The chair provides direction and leadership to the club, dealing with issues as 
and when they arise. 
They are the 'face' of the committee and are intimately involved in all aspects
of club organisation.
This is a pivotal and highly rewarding role which success and impact on the club 
will be determined by your own ambitions and enthusiasms. 
As well as your ability to guide and engage others, it is an opportunity to take 
on a new challenge and influence the future direction of your club.

Day to day jobs include but are not limited to:

- chairing meetings of the committee
- deciding the direction of the club
- setting the goals and vision of the club 
- ensuring the club meets its objectives and vision
- oversee decisions make by the management and other club personnel
- ensure the club operates within the relevant legal frameworks, including Swim England
laws

This varied role can (and does!) require a wide range of skills, including good 
knowledge of the club and competitive swimming, skills in 
organisation, diplomacy, public speaking and more.
The time committment is varied but can be considerable.
Its a challenging role but a massively reqarding one.

## Requirements
- DBS certificate
